oracle.formula: Arrow strength is the variance the edge contributes: strength = beta^2 * Var(parent) (Janzing et al. 2013). Var of a linear-Gaussian root with no parents is sigma^2. A do contrast of width delta is the signed beta*delta.
oracle.note: schema_version 1 pinned strength = abs(beta), which is not a measure of influence because it ignores how much the parent varies. The two edges below are chosen so the two definitions rank them in opposite orders: parent 0 has the smaller coefficient but much the larger variance, and genuinely dominates the child.
asserted_outputs: ranking direction (strength order versus absolute coefficient order)
context_only_outputs: do_contrast block (not read by the executing assertion)
abs_beta_ranking_is_inverted flag as a stored boolean
oracle.independence_basis: The generator reads only the declared sigma, coefficient and delta values and applies strength = beta^2 Var(parent) (Janzing et al. 2013, as stated in the fixture formula) and variance = sigma^2 for a root; it imports no Antecedent code and no statistics package. The shared object is the fixture formula: if the strength definition were misread in both the formula and the generator it would not be detected.
oracle.historical_exposure: The original values were pinned in an earlier import whose harness was not retained; this reference was written during this review from the fixture formula and declared inputs, with the executing assertion read to establish which values it compares and no product implementation source consulted. Who first derived the pinned numbers is unrecorded.

reference_review.scope: Two edges into one child with a large-variance small-coefficient parent and a small-variance large-coefficient parent. The generator recomputes parent variance (sigma squared), edge strength beta^2 Var(parent), the ranking inversion flag and the signed do contrast.
